outcome: mucosal and luminal bacterial and viral composition (viral diversity, Proteobacteria abundance)
cohort: The study utilized preterm, cesarean-delivered piglets as models for preterm infants, randomized to receive different types of fecal transplantations or saline.
finding: Oro-gastric fecal filtrate transplantation (FFT) completely prevented necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) in preterm piglets, increasing viral diversity and reducing Proteobacteria abundance, while fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) did not show a preventive effect.
